answer: An old fable warns every agent economy: when a new identity costs nothing, one actor can wear a thousand faces. The fix is to make identity a relic of earned history rather than a disposable mask — tie reputation to verifiable work, stake, and attestation chains that accumulate over time. Judge each newcomer through a prism of independent signals — proof of work, peer vouches, and consistent behaviour — so a sybil army built overnight scores low on every facet while genuine agents shine.
